questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses inversion in a rhetorical question to emphasise the speaker’s surprise at the situation?
options: It was not until she arrived that we realised the meeting was cancelled.
Only when she left did we understand the importance of the project.
Had she not arrived, we would have missed the deadline by a day.
It was not until the last minute that they decided to cancel their plans.
questions.answer: Only when she left did we understand the importance of the project.

questions.question: Which sentence demonstrates the use of a cleft construction to highlight the subject of a complex statement?
options: What matters most is that we communicate clearly with our team.
The reason for the delay was that the equipment malfunctioned unexpectedly.
It was not until we fixed the issue that we resumed operations.
The fact that he left early surprised everyone.
questions.answer: The reason for the delay was that the equipment malfunctioned unexpectedly.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly employs a third conditional with a subjunctive mood to express a hypothetical scenario?
options: If she had studied harder, she would have passed the exam.
If I were you, I would avoid that restaurant—it’s always overpriced.
Had he known the rules, he wouldn’t have made that mistake.
She wished she had taken the job, but she was too nervous.
questions.answer: If she had studied harder, she would have passed the exam.

questions.question: Which sentence best demonstrates the use of ellipsis in a formal context to maintain conciseness?
options: He left without saying goodbye, and she didn’t blame him.
She wanted to know why he had failed to respond to her emails.
The document, which was due yesterday, was never submitted.
It was clear that he had no intention of helping—he’d made that obvious.
questions.answer: It was clear that he had no intention of helping—he’d made that obvious.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly combines a formal register with a complex conditional structure to express a hypothetical yet urgent situation?
options: Should she arrive late, the conference would be disrupted.
Had they been informed sooner, the crisis could have been averted.
If you had called in advance, we would have prepared the materials.
Unless they acted immediately, the project would be abandoned.
questions.answer: Should she arrive late, the conference would be disrupted.
